panels.figure_caption: Histopathologic image (H&E stain) demonstrating a keratin-filled cyst lined by stratified squamous epithelium with abrupt trichilemmal keratinization, characteristic of a benign pilar cyst. The cyst wall is composed of stratified squamous epithelium with surrounding fibrous connective tissue. No malignant features were identified. Calcification and mitotic activity were not specifically described in the histopathology report.
in_text_mentions: The patient tolerated the procedure well and was discharged home the same day. The pathology report confirmed a benign pilar cyst with no evidence of malignancy, as displayed in Figure 3. Complete excision was achieved intraoperatively. The patient was advised to follow up as needed; however, no subsequent clinical follow-up was documented, and therefore, the long-term postoperative status and recurrence of the lesion could not be assessed.

panels.rationale: Single H&E histology image from trichilemmal cyst of eyelid case. Caption and in-text describe peripheral palisading, swollen inner cells without intercellular bridges, and homogeneous keratin with calcification, matching two vocabulary histology findings for trichilemmal_cyst.

panels.figure_caption: Histopathology of lesion shown in Figure 1. The epithelial lining below shows peripheral palisading of the peripheral cells. Inner cells are swollen. Cyst cavity is filled with homogenous keratin with calcification. (Hematoxylin-eosin ×400).
in_text_mentions: Microscopic examination showed lining keratinized stratified squamous epithelium of eyelid skin. Subepithelium showed a cyst, wall of which was composed of epithelial cells with absence of clearly visible intercellular bridges. The epithelial cells close to the cystic cavity appeared swollen filled with pale cytoplasm. The peripheral layer of cells showed distinct palisade arrangement. Cyst was filled with homogeneous, amorphous keratinous material. Patchy calcification of this keratinous material was noted. Cholesterol clefts were seen at places in the amorphous material (Figures 3 and 4).

panels.rationale: H&E histopathology from a confirmed pilar cyst case showing the cyst wall with abrupt keratinization and absent granular layer, the hallmark trichilemmal (isthmus-catagen) keratinization pattern. Real patient tissue, clear quality, disease attribution supported by caption, in-text description, and article title.

panels.figure_caption: No granular layer is observed at the wall of cyst (H&E). Bar length = 200 μm.
in_text_mentions: There were no obvious abnormalities in blood routine, coagulation and liver and kidney function. A histopathological examination was conducted and the pathology showed that the cyst was in the reticular dermis (Fig. 2), with surrounding basal cells arranged as a fence. The cytoplasm of cells above the basal layer was lightly stained, swollen, and eosinophilic with fuzzy borders. The cells of stratified epithelium lost their nuclei abruptly without an intermediated granular cell layer. The innermost cells seemed to have fallen off into the cavity (Fig. 3).

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph (panel A) of a real human patient. The article title ('Pilar cyst on the dorsum of hand') and caption/in-text ('flesh-colored, dome-shaped nodule on the opisthenar of his right hand') attribute the lesion to a trichilemmal (pilar) cyst. The visible manifestation is a solitary smooth dome-shaped nodule without a punctum, matching the vocabulary's dome-shaped nodule finding; the morphology is classic for trichilemmal cyst, but the extra-scalp dorsal-hand site is a less common location, so typicality is variant. Patient is a 76-year-old man (older_adult); skin is adequately lit and light in tone. No ethnicity is stated. No diagram, control, other-disease, or copyright issue is present. Confidence is high for disease attribution, slightly reduced because the closest vocabulary finding is labeled for the scalp while this lesion is on the hand.
